content.what_it_is: PARALLEL_FIELD_IO provides two distributed field writers (L65-L233). PutFileASCII strips each rank's ghost cells, gathers global index ranges and point-to-point tile data onto world rank 0, assembles PHIGLOB, and writes a formatted field subsampled by OUTPUT_RES (L70-L167). PutFileBinary creates memory and file subarray MPI datatypes for the interior tile and collectively writes every rank's data directly into a shared native-format file (L171-L231).
entities: SUBROUTINE PutFileASCII L70; FILE/PHI L73-L74; rank/count/status locals L81-L83; LocalPHI/xx L85-L86; PHIGLOB L89; saved FirstCallPutFile L91-L92
SUBROUTINE PutFileBinary L171; FILE_NAME/PHI/PHITEST L174-L176; MPI handles/types L178-L181; offset L179

unresolved: ASCII output applies OUTPUT_RES in both J and I loops at L155-L156, but PutFileBinary defines/writes the full interior subarrays at L191-L226 and never references OUTPUT_RES. Selecting FIELD_IO_TYPE therefore changes not only encoding but also spatial resolution and array dimensions, an interface mismatch for the same PutFile caller.

PutFileBinary creates and commits mem_type_loc and file_type_glob on every call at L209-L216 but never calls MPI_TYPE_FREE before returning at L231. Repeated preview output leaks two MPI datatype handles per field and can exhaust MPI resources in long runs.

MPI_FILE_OPEN uses WRONLY+CREATE at L219-L221 without an exclusive/create-new or truncation step. Reusing an existing filename whose expected payload is shorter can leave trailing bytes from the previous file, because the routine writes the current view and closes without setting file size.

PutFileASCII steps DO loops by OUTPUT_RES at L155-L156 with no local range validation. READ_INPUT accepts any integer and provides no positivity check, so OUTPUT_RES=0 is an invalid zero DO increment and negative values produce empty/invalid traversal rather than a controlled error.
